Guidance & outlook: This represents an increase of 19.4% over Q3 FY26.

The EBITDA margin as well expanded to 15.6% in Q4 FY26 compared to 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, once again representing an expansion of 407 basis points year-on-year and 702 basis points sequentially.
15 crores for the quarter, an increase of 64.2% o ver Q4 FY25 and 467.29% over Q3 FY26.
Growth & demand: The business remains positioned to accelerate volume growth as the broader demand environment recovers hopefully in the coming quarters and year ahead.

So, Mitesh can correct me on the factual numbers if I am wrong, but I think we have achieved in the Atlas API, the general pharmaceutical business, a volume growth of about 18% CAGR over the last three years.
But in terms of financial growth and the large volume growth of Pregabalin, it continues to remain a very strong, somewhere around 60%-70% of our business would be for Pregabalin.
Margins & costs: Profit before tax for the full year was INR 25.56 crores against INR 24.98 crores in FY25, a marginal increase of 2.35%.
For both answering on EBITDAs for both the ATC as well as Atlas business, we would guide that Management would like to target EBITDA margin of about 13% of the AZO business.

So, in the Pigment section, the AP C business of AZO, the utilization levels are currently hovering around 65% and there is opportunity to take this utilization levels forward to about 75% to 85% before we are required to push a small CAPEX to increase capacity.
Capex & expansion: At Chattral plant, well, we are going at a utilization level around 70%, which is good for the intermediate level.
So, since acquisition, price has dropped by around 40%-45%.
You had indi cated in the past that once utilization is 85%, capacity expansion would be triggered.
Balance sheet & cash: 3.30 crores in Q4, down 14.15% ye ar-on-year, reflecting our ongoing debt reduction.
EBITDA positivity in both the AZO and API segments, continued deleveraging of the balance sheet and maintenance of PAT growth are the principal outcomes of the year.
Secondly, we as a group and as a company are very decently positioned because we have over the last four years completed our entire CAPEX cycle where our debt also rose to a total peak debt of Rs.
Risks & challenges: These risks and uncertainties have been entailed in our annual reports.
The operating environment continues to present challenges, with raw material prices remaining elevated and global supply chains having seen a lot of disruption.
Since COVID, the whole period of last three to four years has been extremely challenging now with the disruptions of the US-Iran war and oil disruptions and raw material disruptions.
